description: Computes servicer-compliance due dates and clock states from event dates and loan values: error-resolution and information-request clocks, loss-mitigation acknowledgment and evaluation, the 37-day pre-sale boundary, the 120-day pre-foreclosure bar, no-duplicate processing, force-placed-insurance notice, reminder, cancel and refund clocks, payment-crediting and payoff-statement deadlines, and ARM notice windows with their exception branches. Every obligation carries its paragraph citation and a named business-day calendar assumption. Invalid dates, removed rule branches and over-bound event sets are refused, never computed.

cited_clause_digest.clause_path: 12 CFR 1024.35(d), (e)(3)(i)(A)-(C), (e)(3)(ii) -- error resolution: 5-business-day acknowledgment; 7-business-day, sale-bounded, and 30-business-day investigation windows; 15-business-day extension
12 CFR 1024.36(c), (d)(2)(i)(A)-(B), (d)(2)(ii) -- information requests: 5-business-day acknowledgment; 10-business-day owner-identity and 30-business-day general windows; 15-business-day extension

12 CFR 1024.41(b)(2)(i), (c)(1), (f)(1)(i), (g), (i) -- loss mitigation: 5-business-day acknowledgment (45-day gate), 30-day evaluation behind the 37-day pre-sale threshold, 120-day pre-foreclosure bar, no-duplicate rule; post-IFR text only (90 FR 20792, May 16, 2025)
12 CFR 1024.37(c)(1)(i), (d)(1), (g) -- force-placed insurance: 45-day advance notice, reminder notice 30 days after the initial notice and 15 days before the charge, 15-day cancel-and-refund clock
12 CFR 1026.36(c)(1)(i), (c)(1)(iii), (c)(3) -- payment crediting as of date of receipt and five days after receipt for accepted non-conforming payments; payoff statement within seven business days

12 CFR 1026.20(c)(2), (d) -- ARM notice windows: 60-120 days before the first payment at the adjusted level; 25-day floor for fast-cycle and pre-2015 short-index ARMs and for the estimated-rate first adjustment within 60 days of consummation; 210-240 days for the initial adjustment with the at-consummation case
